FilesTable.description:
File-to-source-kind glob mapping (ryl-only; TOML). Each kind selects which
files are linted as that kind. A file matching more than one kind is an error.

markdown.description: Glob patterns for markdown files whose embedded YAML is linted.

yaml.description: Glob patterns for files linted directly as YAML.

FixRuleName.description: A fixable rule name accepted by `lint.unfixable`.

FixTable.description: The deprecated `[fix]` table; its keys now live in `[lint]`.

document-end.description: Whether to add a missing `...` document end marker.

document-start.description: Whether to add a missing `---` document start marker.

fold-long-lines.description: Whether to split plain scalar lines longer than `line-length` at single spaces.

quote-style.description: Preferred quote for strings that need quoting; `preserve` leaves quoting alone.

KeyOrderEntry.description: A configured key order for the mappings that both `files` and `path` select.

per-line-ignores.description: Per-line rule ignores: suppress rules on lines/files matching a pattern.

MarkdownTable.description: Markdown embedding behaviour. ryl-only (TOML); yamllint has no equivalent.

fenced-blocks.description: Lint fenced `yaml`/`yml` code blocks. Defaults to `true`.

front-matter.description: Lint the leading YAML front matter block. Defaults to `true`.

OutputDestination.description:
Where one format's output goes. An absent `path` means the format's default stream
(stderr for the console formats, stdout for `junit`/`gitlab`); `"-"` means stdout; any
other value is a file path.

OutputTable.description:
Output targets (ryl-only; TOML). Each format present is rendered to its destination,
so several formats produce several outputs in one run (e.g. console plus a report
file). A CLI `--format` overrides this table wholesale. yamllint has no equivalent;
see `docs/output-formats.md`.

auto.description: Auto-detected console format (GitHub annotations in CI, otherwise colored/plain).

PerLineIgnore.description:
A single `per-line-ignores` entry. Suppresses `rules` on source lines matching
`regex` (the whole physical line, unanchored) within files matching `path` (a
glob). All present fields must match (logical AND); at least one of `regex`/`path`
is required (validated in `validate_toml_config`), so an entry can't disable a rule
globally.
